strategy_objective_guidance:
- Single scored quantity: `combined_score = (dmin/dmax)^2 / (1/4.165849767)`. No other terms; runtime is reported but not scored (only the implicit timeout). Score is uncapped, so beating the reference (score > 1) is possible and is the only lever.
- Hard constraints: return a finite NumPy array of exactly shape (14, 3); dmax > 0. Any exception → score 0, so robustness (always returning a valid incumbent) is essential but not itself scored.
- The objective is scale/translation/rotation invariant — only the *ratio* matters. Equivalently: maximize t s.t. d(i,j)² ≥ t and d(i,j)² ≤ 1 for all pairs — a smooth constrained NLP with 91 pairwise constraints in 42 variables.
- No conflicting weighted terms; the only tradeoff is dmin up vs dmax down, both captured in one ratio. The largest remaining lever is purely geometric: finding a better 14-point packing (best-known squared ratio slightly above 1/4.1658 ≈ 0.24).
- The program receives no input at all — it must *construct* the point set offline. Full batch/offline global optimization is permitted; no streaming/causality concerns. Precomputation inside the function is fine within the timeout.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Symmetric polyhedral constructions: build candidates from icosahedral/dodecahedral symmetry groups, e.g., vertices of the icosahedron plus face/edge centers, or two rotated rings; scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation for generating symmetric orbits; score each with scipy.spatial.distance.pdist. These give strong deterministic incumbents.
- Max-min constrained NLP: maximize t with constraints d(i,j)² − t ≥ 0 and 1 − d(i,j)² ≥ 0 via scipy.optimize.minimize(method="SLSQP") on a smooth reformulation (minimize −t). Direct, differentiable, handles the 91 constraints natively.
- Smooth-min surrogate + unconstrained descent: minimize −logsumexp(−d(i,j)²/τ) + penalty on max distance using scipy.optimize.minimize(method="L-BFGS-B" or "BFGS") with annealed τ; gradient-friendly, avoids constraint machinery.
- Deterministic multistart local search: many seeded starts (fixed RNG seed, random normal points normalized to unit diameter), each polished by SLSQP, keep best ratio; scipy.cluster or simple greedy perturbation (move the point achieving dmin outward along the direction away from its nearest neighbor) as a zeroth-order fallback.
- Differential evolution / global search: scipy.optimize.differential_evolution on a reduced parametrization (e.g., symmetry-reduced coordinates or spherical angles), budget-limited; use as an independent family when local methods stall in poor basins.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Active-set polish: after local optimization, identify the pairs attaining dmin and dmax; re-run SLSQP warm-started at the incumbent with only those active constraints tightened — typically gains the last few 1e-3.
- Symmetry breaking / parametrization reduction: fix one point at origin, another on an axis, optimize only the remaining free DOFs (or group orbits under a chosen symmetry) — shrinks the search space and speeds convergence without changing the attainable ratio.
- Scale normalization as convenience: after each optimization step rescale so dmax = 1 (project points back into the unit-diameter feasible set) so the constraint d² ≤ 1 stays satisfied; keeps intermediate iterates valid.
- Multistart budget tuning: e.g., 50–200 starts with seed fixed (np.random.default_rng(0)), each capped at ~200 SLSQP iterations, ftol/xtol ~1e-12; keep the best valid array — total runtime kept well under timeout.
- Fallback guard: wrap all numerics in try/except; always return the best symmetric-construction incumbent (precomputed at module load or first computed deterministically) if any optimizer fails, guaranteeing shape (14,3), finiteness, and dmax > 0.

strategies.title: [epigraph-slsqp] Epigraph max-min NLP with SLSQP and active-set continuation
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: epigraph-slsqp
Replacement scope: Replace the entire `_soft_step` + `_refine` pipeline inside `_optimize` (the softmin/softmax ascent and the subgradient polish) with a single SLSQP solve of the epigraph NLP; keep the multistart loop and fallback structure of `min_max_dist_dim3_14` as-is.
Compute budget: ≤ 60 starts (existing polyhedral seeds + fixed-seed random starts, `np.random.default_rng(0)`), each SLSQP capped at 300 iterations with ftol/xtol 1e-12 on 43 variables (42 coordinates + t) and 182 constraints; expected evaluation time ≤ 8 s, well within the incumbent's ~7 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's subgradient polish converges to a non-smooth stationary point of the ratio with no feasibility machinery, so it cannot jointly enforce "all 91 pairwise squared distances ≥ t" and "all ≤ 1" while pushing t up; the epigraph formulation makes t an explicit decision variable with analytic gradients (∇ of d(i,j)² is linear in coordinates), which directly targets the exact scored quantity and typically recovers the last 1e-2–2e-2 of squared ratio that soft surrogates leave on the table. Formulation: variables (P flattened, t), minimize −t, constraints d(i,j)² − t ≥ 0 and 1 − d(i,j)² ≥ 0; after each solve, run one warm-started continuation pass keeping only constraints within 1% of active (active-set refinement) for ≤ 100 extra iterations. Hard validity: every returned candidate is checked with `_ratio` before acceptance; the best valid incumbent is kept; on any SLSQP failure the previous incumbent is returned, so shape (14,3), finiteness, and dmax > 0 always hold.
Expected-gain check: the reference squared ratio 1/4.165849767 ≈ 0.240045 is an explicitly attainable value for this NLP, and the incumbent's 0.216021 is strictly below it, so a converged epigraph solve over the same 14-point feasible set must, at minimum, match configurations known to exist at 0.240045 — i.e., a falsifiable threshold of combined_score ≥ 1.0 (raw min_max_ratio ≥ 0.240045) strictly exceeding the current 0.8999.

strategies.title: [staggered-ring-orbit] Symmetry-reduced two-ring construction (7+7 staggered rin
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: staggered-ring-orbit
Replacement scope: Replace the seed list in `min_max_dist_dim3_14` (cube+octahedron, icosahedron+poles, random starts) with a parametric family of two-ring configurations, and optimize the few ring parameters directly instead of perturbing all 42 coordinates.
Compute budget: ≤ 200 parametric starts (deterministic grid over ring heights and twist angles plus 20 seeded L-BFGS-B polishes of the ≤ 6 ring parameters, ≤ 400 iterations each); expected evaluation time ≤ 3 s added, total under timeout.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's seeds have contact topologies (cube/octahedron orbits, icosahedron orbits) whose best local optima are structurally capped below the reference; the best-known 14-point spherical configurations have a different contact topology — two horizontal rings of 7 points each at heights ±h, with a relative twist angle θ (staggered antiprism-like), optionally with the rings at unequal radii. Parametrize: ring 1 at z = +h, azimuths 2πk/7; ring 2 at z = −h, azimuths 2πk/7 + θ; free parameters (h, θ, and optionally two radii r1, r2 and a global stretch) — about 4–6 DOFs instead of 42. Optimize (dmin/dmax)² over these DOFs with scipy L-BFGS-B (analytic gradients of squared distances in the parameters), then hand the best configuration to the existing `_refine` for a short full-DOF polish (≤ 1000 iterations). This is a genuinely different geometric seed family with a contact graph (7 nearest neighbors per point within its ring plus staggered inter-ring contacts) that the incumbent's polyhedral seeds cannot reach by local moves. Hard validity: all candidates are explicit finite coordinates; each is scored with `_ratio` and kept only if better; the incumbent fallback is untouched.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the 7-fold staggered-ring contact topology with twist angle θ, which the incumbent's cube/icosahedron orbits cannot realize under any local perturbation (their symmetry orders are 4, 6, and 12, not 7), and the falsifiable threshold is raw min_max_ratio ≥ 0.240045 (combined_score ≥ 1.0), strictly above the incumbent's 0.216021.

strategies.title: [de-angular-global] Differential evolution on symmetry-reduced spherical coordin
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: de-angular-global
Replacement scope: Replace the perturbation-restart phase at the end of `min_max_dist_dim3_14` (the fixed-seed Gaussian perturbations around the incumbent) with a differential-evolution global search over a reduced angular parametrization, keeping the best-of-all-phases selection and fallback.
Compute budget: one `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` run with maxiter ≤ 150, popsize ≤ 20, seed 0, polish=True (L-BFGS-B), on a reduced parametrization of ≤ 30 variables; expected evaluation time ≤ 5 s, within timeout.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's escape mechanism is isotropic Gaussian perturbation of all 42 coordinates, which cannot jump between contact topologies — it only re-descends into the same or nearby basins. Differential evolution over spherical angles (θ_i, φ_i for 14 points, with point 0 fixed at the north pole and point 1 constrained to a meridian to remove rotation invariance, giving 26 free angles) performs population-level recombination that crosses basin boundaries and discovers contact graphs neither the polyhedral seeds nor the local polish can reach. Objective for DE: −(dmin/dmax)² computed with `scipy.spatial.distance.pdist` on the unit sphere (scale-invariant, so no diameter constraint needed inside DE); the DE result is then polished with the existing `_refine` for ≤ 1500 iterations and accepted only if it beats the incumbent by the exact `_ratio`. Hard validity: DE output is converted to Cartesian coordinates, checked for finiteness and dmax > 0, and the incumbent is returned whenever DE fails or does not improve.
Expected-gain check: the precise new degree of freedom is population-based recombination across the full angular configuration space (a global escape direction), which the incumbent's local perturbation restarts provably cannot supply since they are confined to the incumbent's basin; the falsifiable threshold is any raw min_max_ratio strictly above the post-SLSQP incumbent, with the explicit target 0.240045 (combined_score ≥ 1.0) versus the current 0.216021.

strategies.title: [ico-orbit-seeds] Icosahedral/dodecahedral orbit seeds replacing the 7+7 ring po
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ico-orbit-seeds
Replacement scope: The seed-generation block in `min_max_dist_dim3_14()` (the `_ring_config` grid pool and the L-BFGS-B ring search) is replaced by a deterministic family of icosahedral-symmetry seeds; the existing `_soft_step` → `_epigraph_solve` polish pipeline and `_consider` guard are kept unchanged and applied to each new seed.
Compute budget: ~25 deterministic seeds, each one short polish (soft_iters ≤ 300, epigraph rounds ≤ 4, maxiter ≤ 400), plus seeded jitters around the best two seeds (≤ 20 total). Expected evaluation time comparable to or below the current ~4.3 s since the expensive ring grid is dropped.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's entire search lives in the two-congruent-7-gon basin; its contact topology is ring-neighbor-dominated. Icosahedral seeds have a different contact graph: (a) 12 icosahedron vertices + 2 points on a common 5-fold axis (free height parameter), (b) 12 vertices + 2 antipodal face centers, (c) 20 dodecahedron-face-centers reduced to 14 by keeping two full 5-fold orbits plus 4 equatorial points, (d) icosahedron vertices + edge-midpoint orbit truncated to 14. These seeds start closer to packings whose dmin/dmax can exceed the ring ceiling; the epigraph NLP then only has to break symmetry locally rather than discover a new topology. Validity is preserved because every seed is finite and `_consider` accepts only exact-ratio improvements, with the current ring incumbent retained as an additional seed in the pool so the returned array is never worse than the incumbent's.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the icosahedral contact topology (each vertex has 5 nearest neighbors at equal distance, versus the ring's mixed 2+2 neighbor structure); the incumbent's 7+7 parametrization cannot represent it, and if any ico-orbit seed polishes to a squared ratio above the incumbent's 0.239913 the combined score strictly exceeds 0.999441 — falsifiable by running the same pipeline on seed (a) alone.

strategies.title: [unequal-twisted-rings] Unequal staggered rings (6+8, 5+9, 4+10) with independen
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: unequal-twisted-rings
Replacement scope: Replace `_ring_config` and its bounds/grid with a generalized two-ring parametrization supporting unequal ring sizes k and 14−k at heights ±h with independent radii r1, r2 and relative twist θ; keep the L-BFGS-B reduced search, `_polish`, and `_consider` infrastructure as-is.
Compute budget: for k ∈ {4,5,6} run the same coarse deterministic grid (~60 starts, maxiter 400 L-BFGS-B on 4 DOFs), polish the top ~5 per k, plus ≤ 10 seeded jitters per k. Expected evaluation time roughly equal to the current run.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent forces two congruent 7-gons, which fixes the angular spacing to 2π/7 on both rings and makes within-ring nearest-neighbor distances the binding constraint. Unequal rings relax the constraint that the two rings have identical angular spacing: with k=6 and 14−k=8, the 8-ring can sit at a different radius so that inter-ring chord distances match within-ring chords at the optimum, a balance the 7+7 family cannot strike (its two rings are forced to share spacing). This is a genuinely new geometric DOF (the ring-size split), not a reparameterization. Hard validity is preserved by the unchanged finite-seed construction plus the exact-ratio acceptance guard, with the 7+7 incumbent included in the candidate pool.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the independent angular spacings 2π/k and 2π/(14−k) with independent radii; the incumbent's parametrization provably cannot realize a configuration where within-ring chord length on one ring differs from the other, and the strategy is falsified if no k≠7 split polishes above squared ratio 0.239913 (combined 0.999441).

strategies.title: [antipodal-pair-orbit] 7-antipodal-pairs construction (centrally symmetric 14-po
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: antipodal-pair-orbit
Replacement scope: Replace the seed pool in `min_max_dist_dim3_14()` with a centrally symmetric construction: 14 points as 7 antipodal pairs ±v_i on (or near) the unit sphere, parametrized by 7 unit directions with symmetry-reduced spherical coordinates (fix v_1 = north pole, v_2 in the xz-plane, leaving 19 free DOFs), optimized by seeded L-BFGS-B on the exact ratio with per-pair radius as one extra scalar per pair; the existing epigraph polish and `_consider` guard remain the refinement stage.
Compute budget: ≤ 40 deterministic multistarts (fixed seed) with maxiter 300 each on the ≤ 26-variable reduced problem, top 8 polished via `_epigraph_solve` (rounds ≤ 4). Expected evaluation time within the current budget since the reduced problem is much smaller than 42 variables.
Gain mechanism: Central symmetry forces every diameter pair to distance exactly 2 (a natural dmax candidate set of 7 pairs) and makes the max-min problem equivalent to choosing 7 lines through the origin maximizing the minimum pairwise line angle — a compact, well-studied line-packing structure with a contact topology (each point's farthest neighbor is its antipode) that the ring and ico seeds do not enforce. The incumbent cannot represent a configuration where all 7 diameters are exactly maximal simultaneously. Per-pair radii slightly below 1 (one extra scalar each) let the optimizer trade diameter shrinkage against chord growth, escaping the pure-sphere restriction. Validity: all seeds are finite by construction, dmax = 2 > 0, and the exact-ratio guard plus retained incumbent fallback guarantee a valid (14,3) return.
Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the centrally symmetric contact topology (7 simultaneous antipodal dmax pairs and line-angle-based dmin), which the 7+7 ring and ico-orbit parametrizations cannot express; the strategy is falsified if the best polished antipodal configuration stays at or below squared ratio 0.239913 (combined 0.999441).
